result:
I played all 24 months. All three training runs were met, no inference demand went unserved, and there were no penalties. **Net cost: $1,003.1M.**

| | $M |
|---|---|
| GPU purchases (44k gen H, all bought in months 0–3) | 755.0 |
| Power | 196.2 |
| Reserved cloud contracts | 216.8 |
| Spot | 29.9 |
| Interest | 32.7 |
| GPU resales | −42.9 |
| Value of GPUs still held at the end | −263.3 |
| Contract and power payments still owed after month 23 | +78.7 |

**How it went**
- **Buying early:** I bought gen H in months 0–3 while supply looked loose. Owning worked out cheaper per kH-month than reserving cloud capacity. Broker A delivered the one test order I placed.
- **Gen N launch:** the rumours only all fit one month, 18, and that was right. So I didn't buy gen N, since it would only have been usable for months 21–23. Instead I timed the window 3 cloud reservations for months 14–18, the last one after the launch price cut. I bought spot only in the cheap months ($0.65–0.85M per kH-month).
- **Inference:** demand grew about 7% a month and reached roughly 28 kH. I added 14 MW of power so all the gen H stayed running after the original 16 MW contract ended in month 19.

**What I'd change:** I overbuilt for the first two runs. They finished at 136/60 and 254/140 kH-months, so much of the compute in months 5–7 and 13–15 went unused. The 12k gen H order in month 3 could probably have been smaller or later, with reservations covering more of window 3. That would have cut the GPU spend and some of the interest. Window 3 ended at 331/320, a reasonable safety margin given the $200M penalty for a miss.

I recorded the belief log with `note` every month. My first note got split in two because I used semicolons inside it, which the command line treats as separators, so the month 0 entry is only partly recorded. The later notes avoid semicolons.
